A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COVec, with matching authors, method, and original experiments. Their complete text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction experiments on Face, Scene, and Emoji datasets, including MSE/LPIPS curves in Figure 7, editing comparisons, and ablations in Figures 11–14.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds Vector Compactness results in Table 1 and CLIPScore comparisons in Figure 15.

M1.justification: Initialization, structural optimization, illumination refinement, layer separation, and the simplified emoji variant remain unchanged. Section 4.2 clarifies that mask grouping occurs independently within each layer, without establishing a change to the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Face images from FFHQ, Scene images from Things/TID2013, Emoji images from Noto Emoji, and color-editing evaluations. V2's new metrics evaluate the existing Face and Scene datasets without introducing another task or population.

E2.justification: DiffVG, LIVE, O&R, and LayerVec remain the comparison methods. V2's Table 1 and Figure 15 use this same set, and the binarization alternatives in the existing ablation remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix A adds VeC evaluation using four randomly sampled semantic masks per image and an overlap threshold above 85%. It also adds BLIP-generated reference captions and CLIP similarity measurements across 8–256 paths. Existing reconstruction and editing protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The albedo-initialization, binarization, and loss ablations in Section 5.3 and the appendix editing and layer-representation examples are retained. Appendix A adds comparative metric scores, without a new ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study.

E5.justification: V2's Table 1 newly reports average and standard-deviation rows for VeC on both datasets. The aggregation underlying the standard deviations is not explicitly explained, and no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports COVec VeC means of 65.2% on Face and 66.2% on Scene, compared with LayerVec's 55.4% and 57.6%. New Figure 15 reports competitive CLIPScore curves across path budgets. The original MSE/LPIPS curves and qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), the intrinsic-image assumptions, and the appendix layer-separation and color-editing mathematics are retained. The added evaluation descriptions introduce no new theoretical result, formal derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about intrinsic decomposition in vector graphics, region-wise semantic binarization, visual fidelity, semantic conciseness, and editability. The new appendix evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A adds interpretations linking VeC to containment within semantic object boundaries and rendered-image CLIP similarity to stable layer-wise semantic alignment across path budgets. Existing mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications remain unchanged; no new limitations are discussed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a prospective code-release location in the abstract and explicitly clarifies independent mask grouping within each layer. Appendix A documents mask sampling, the overlap threshold, and BLIP caption generation for its new evaluations. The code is promised, rather than established as available.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to CLIPScore and BLIP for the new evaluation and cites the already included LayerVec work for VeC. The related-work discussion and positioning relative to earlier vectorization and intrinsic-decomposition methods remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds an opening quantitative-results appendix, acknowledgements, and a brief mask-grouping clarification. Existing appendices are renumbered, and 'Additional Results' becomes 'Additional Qualitative Results'; the main narrative is largely unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 1 and the two-panel CLIPScore Figure 15, and refreshes the rendering of pipeline Figure 4. Existing appendix Figures 15–19 become Figures 16–20 with unchanged visual content, alongside limited layout and pagination shifts.

improvement.justification: Appendix A adds quantitative support for semantic organization, which v1 demonstrated mainly through qualitative examples: VeC comparisons include dispersion, and CLIPScore curves assess semantic fidelity across path budgets. This strengthens the evidence modestly. The gain remains limited because the VeC path budget and standard-deviation aggregation are unspecified, and rendered-image CLIP similarity does not directly establish individual-layer correctness.
